verdict.reasoning: Patient says, "I've been having this blinding headache for a few days" and later clarifies it started "three days ago" and that pain is "kind of all over, but...over my right eye is a bit stronger."
Headache duration and description: "I've been having this blinding headache for a few days" and "that was three days ago" with location "over my right eye is a bit stronger."
Onset and persistence: "It just started all of a sudden. I woke up one morning with a headache" and "I just keep having. It doesn't really go away without ibuprofen either."
Effect of ibuprofen and pain scores: patient says ibuprofen makes it "a bit better" and rates severity: "I guess it's mostly eight, and then it comes down to maybe a five."
Photophobia: In response to light tolerance, patient says, "Lights definitely make me more sensitive. I don't really like strong lights."
Visual symptoms: patient reports, "yeah, vision. I think I get this shooting light sometimes... just a bit of a weird kind of vision."
Nausea/vomiting: patient answers, "No, I'm feeling a bit sick, but no vomiting."
Neurological symptoms: when asked about tingling/numbness/weakness, patient replies, "No."
Sinus/URI symptoms: physician asks about "cold symptoms, sore throat, sore ears or pain over the sinuses, any or phlegm, any nosebleeds or cough", and patient replies, "No."
Fever: patient says, "No, I didn't [check temperature], but I don't really feel feverish or anything," and clinician notes she hasn't had a high temperature.
Past abdominal pain: patient states, "I think I only had the abdominal pain when I was younger, but no cause was found and that went away."
Oral contraceptive: patient says she takes "Just the pill"; when asked which, she answers "Marcelone" and that she started it "About a year ago."
Ibuprofen use: "apart from the ibuprofen I take sometimes and the headache gets really bad, so."
Family history: patient states, "my mum suffers from, like, she has migraines" and clarifies, "she has quite bad migraines. She's like. Has the vomiting and everything."
Living situation: when asked who she lives with, patient replies, "Just by myself."
Smoking: in response to "And do you smoke?" patient says, "No."
Alcohol: patient reports, "Probably like three beers once a week."
No vitals (e.g., BP, HR, temp) are mentioned anywhere in the transcript; only history is taken and future checking of BP is planned.
No actual physical examination findings are documented; clinician states they "should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes" in future, implying none done yet.
Clinician says, "it could possibly be a migraine type headache"; patient has photophobia (light sensitivity), "shooting light" visual symptoms, and a maternal history of migraines with vomiting.

Clinician links pill and migraine: "Because if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights..." and explains that with regular migraines with flashing lights the current pill "wouldn't be suitable to stay on."
Red flags: patient denies numbness/weakness ("No"), has "no vomiting," and reports no feverish feeling; no focal neurological deficits or other red flags are described or elicited.
Clinician states, "I can prescribe you something similar to ibuprofen, but a bit stronger... and you can take paracetamol at the same time... take it with food."
Clinician plans, "we probably should book you into an appointment to get an examination. Obviously... we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well."
Future BP and pill review: "When you have an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well, just to make sure your pill is still appropriate for you."

Safety-netting: clinician advises, "if in the meantime, before your appointment, your headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing, then if it's that bad, then you should go to AE and have an examination."

Follow-up: the planned appointment is "for us to do a full examination" including neuro and eye exam, and later, "we'll check your blood pressure as well, just to make sure your pill is still appropriate for you."
